How to get the Ratel exotic AR in Echoes of Central Park, and everything about the Guardians: how to spawn all 6, how to beat every single one, the build that kills them in seconds, and the new Apex Protocol gear set.

Quick reference:
• 6 Guardians: the Howl Pulse boss ends the Central Park main mission (and unlocks the game mode). The other 5 live in the Central Park mode: Corrosive Trap, Leech Hive, Blackout Seeker, Trophy System and Gas Bomber.
• Spawn: find the lair in a zone, kill NPCs until the meter on your shoulder is full, wound the Guardian, reach the lair before the timer runs out, clear the NPCs there and he spawns. Kill him and you unlock his skill.
• Every Guardian has the same weakness: destroy his skill, then burst him in the damage window.
• Build: Prima Donna + 4 Aces & Eights + Iron Will + Melon Baller. Normal gear works, your prototype gear is normalized in Central Park.
• Kill all 5 and Contaminated unlocks. Your first full clear in Contaminated gives the Ratel guaranteed, after that it's a chance per run.
• Every finished run: 8 exotic components + 3 exotic caches. My runs took about 15–20 minutes.
• Ratel (Voracious): more amplified damage the more armor and health the enemy has lost, 1 stack per 100 weapon hits, max 4.

The NEW Ratel Exotic Assault Rifle has arrived in The Division 2: Echoes of Central Park, and this weapon is definitely something different!

In today’s video, we’re taking a closer look at the Ratel, exploring its unique Exotic talent, Voracious, and understanding how this unusual weapon is intended to function. This isn’t your typical run-and-gun Exotic, and getting the most out of it requires a different approach.

So, how does Voracious work?

* Every 100 weapon hits grants 1 stack.
* You can build up to 4 stacks.
* Each stack provides +20% maximum amplified damage and +15% reload speed.
* At maximum stacks, that’s up to 80% maximum amplified damage and 60% reload speed.
* The damage amplification scales with the amount of armor and health an enemy has lost.
* Stacks begin to decay after 3 seconds without shooting or reloading.

Ratel Exotic Weapon Stats & Mods:

* Optic: +15% Critical Hit Chance.
* Magazine: +20 Rounds.
* Underbarrel: +10% Weapon Handling.
* Third attribute: Randomized, with Damage to Targets Out of Cover being an interesting option.

The Ratel shares its base weapon stats with the high-end Honey Badger, but its Exotic talent and weapon modifications give it a completely different identity.

We’ll also explore how to maintain its stacks, understand its damage potential, and approach combat encounters in a way that makes the most of this weapon.

Echoes of Central Park DLC

The newest DLC takes Agents into the Upper West Side and Central Park in New York, introducing a darker, horror-inspired experience with a new campaign, three companions, six new skill variants, a new gear set, and the Ratel Exotic.

There’s plenty of new content to explore, and this is just one of the new additions worth taking a closer look at.

If you’re still trying to understand this Exotic or wondering how to get the most out of its unusual talent, hopefully this video gives you a better understanding of what makes the Ratel so interesting.

Thanks for watching, Agents!

I tested the new Apex Protocol gear set on stream, and two things in it don't work the way the tooltip says. The bonus stacks can't be refreshed, so they're gone when the 30 seconds run out. And with two Guardian skills equipped, the base stacks don't decay at all, which actually helps you. Here's how the set works, what's bugged, what works (the chest's Veer Override amp), and why I'm stashing it until the refresh is fixed.

Quick reference:
• 2-piece: +10% weapon damage, +10% skill damage. 3-piece: +15% weapon handling, +15% hazard protection.
• Apex Engine (4-piece): weapon hits build base stacks. At 100 they're consumed for one bonus stack: +1 skill tier, +65% weapon damage for 30 s, and -10 s on active skill cooldowns. Max 3 bonus stacks, so on paper that's +3 skill tiers and +195% weapon damage.
• Base stack decay: the tooltip says 10 stacks every 5 s, and 5 less with two Guardian skills. In my test, two Guardian skills means no decay at all.
• Bug 1 (helps you): with two Guardian skills, base stacks don't decay.
• Bug 2 (hurts you): bonus stacks don't refresh. Three bonus stacks vanish when the timer runs out.
• Chest Veer Override (needs Apex Engine): at max stacks, enemies hit by your skills are marked for 10 s, and marked enemies take +20% amplified damage. The +20% works in my test. Not every enemy got marked in real content.
• Backpack Veer Failsafe (needs Apex Engine): +5% armor on kill and +10% skill damage per bonus stack.
• Guardian skills come from the Guardians in Central Park. How to get every one: [LÄNK GUARDIANS-GUIDEN]

Full build video when the refresh is fixed. Until then: stash it.

Welcome to Echoes of Central Park, the latest DLC expansion for The Division 2!

With the introduction of a new map, dangerous enemies, and a darker atmosphere, Central Park brings an entirely new challenge for Division agents. Among its biggest challenges are the five Guardians scattered throughout the map.

* Fast boss eliminations and coordinated damage.
* A look at the different Guardian abilities and mechanics.
* Tips for making these encounters quicker and easier.

MEET THE GUARDIANS

Each Guardian brings something different to the battlefield:

* Hollow: Leech Hive and foam-based attacks.
* Mire: Corrosive Trap and increased damage modifiers.
* Specter: Blackout Seeker and dangerous close-range damage.
* Thorn: Trophy System and defensive combat mechanics.
* Vulture: Gas Chamber and poison-based attacks.

Whether you’re looking to farm Guardian rewards, collect the new skill variants, or simply complete these encounters more efficiently, this run should give you a good idea of what’s possible with just two agents.

7ncllv.text:
How to get The Ratel, the new Exotic assault rifle from Echoes of Central Park, the easy way. I explain it in Dutch (English subtitles), then we go through the five Guardians: what each one drops on the first kill and what to watch out for, with footage from my own run. At the end, the Jockkie character sings the Ratel song.

The steps
1. Kill the Guardians the first time: you get their first skill set.
2. Then the map resets and you get Containment mode. You have 24 hours to clear all five lairs, so stay in the park until the last kill.
3. Kill them again. Go straight to the red lairs and skip the meter. Guardians get bonus armor in Containment: disable their deployed skills and hit them in the opening.
4. The Ratel is yours. The first full clear guarantees the Exotic, on any difficulty.
5. Want to be stronger on the way? Use the Emerald nodes (Veer Override) and stay on the map to keep the buff.

The Guardians
- Hollow: Leech Hive (80% damage reduction while it is active), throws 3 foam grenades
- Mire: Corrosive Trap (a triggered trap buffs his damage by 500% for 15 seconds)
- Specter: Blackout Seeker (within 15 meters his damage is 500% higher)
- Thorn: Trophy System
- Vulture: Gas Chamber (poisoned targets cannot sprint, 300% damage from 15 meters)
Every Guardian is weak to Disrupt. Each Guardian drops a skill variant on the first kill.

Golden Bullet is back in The Division 2, and this time it's better than ever! Ubisoft has introduced new buffs, a fresh co-op mechanic, and an exclusive free mask for Agents who complete the Global Event challenges.

The Golden Bullet buff now grants a massive one hundred percent Weapon Damage increase. But there's another major addition: Golden Link. When you score kills while using Golden Bullet, you fill a meter that can share a powerful buff with nearby teammates who don't currently have Golden Bullet.

Golden Link provides fifty percent Weapon Damage, one hundred percent Weapon Handling, and ten percent Rate of Fire. This creates a new opportunity for coordinated teams to spread the firepower and make the most of the event's combat bonuses.

There's also a brand-new reward waiting at Tier Ten: the Lead Catcher Mask! In this video, we break down the updated Golden Bullet mechanics, the new team buff, the weapon bonuses, and how to earn the free mask.

1ve6gvw.text:
Legendary Open World is coming to Washington, D.C.! Year Eight Season Four is raising the difficulty in Tom Clancy’s The Division 2, bringing Legendary difficulty to the open world and introducing four additional Legendary Main Missions.

Agents will be able to set their Global Difficulty to Legendary and face the White Tusk throughout Washington, D.C. They'll take over Control Points and appear in activities including Propaganda Broadcasts, Territory Controls, Public Executions, Resource Convoys, Aerial Convoys, Rescue Operations, and Supply Drops. Other enemy factions will also receive increased health and damage.

Four Main Missions are getting the Legendary treatment: Air and Space Museum, Space Administration HQ, Grand Washington Hotel, and ViewPoint Museum. Each mission features reworked White Tusk encounters designed to challenge even highly optimized builds.

Legendary Projects are also changing. The Daily Legendary Mission Project will refresh every day, and completing three Daily Legendary Mission Projects during the same weekly cycle will unlock an additional reward package. Legendary missions will also offer opportunities to earn Prototype Gear, although the drop rates shown during the Public Test Server are temporary.

nnnbor.text:
Prototype Gear is getting a major overhaul in The Division 2 Year 8 Season 4! Ubisoft is giving Agents something they've been asking for: the ability to choose their own Augments instead of relying on random rerolls. This could completely change how we build and optimize our endgame gear.

With the new Select Augment feature, you can visit the ProtoLab, browse the available Augments, and choose exactly which one you want for your Prototype item. Changing an Augment costs a fixed amount of Prototype Cores, but here's the best part: your Augment upgrade progress stays with the item! If you've upgraded an Augment to level five, switching to another Augment won't reset that progress.

Year Eight Season Four is also introducing Prototype Schematics, a new customization system that replaces traditional Recalibration and Optimization for Prototype items. Depending on the Schematic, you can replace eligible attributes, adjust attribute values, add bonus attributes, or change eligible talents. You'll be able to unlock Schematics through Prototype Requisition Vendor caches, missions, and Legendary bosses.

mp1q2d.text:
The Division 2 Red, Blue, and Yellow builds are getting brand-new abilities in Year 8 Season 4! The new Core Build Escalation Directive changes how your build performs in combat, rewarding you for playing to the strengths of your chosen Core. Whether you're a damage dealer, a tank, or a skill-focused Agent, your build now determines the abilities you bring to the fight.

With the Red Core, you'll deal more damage at longer ranges. Build stacks by dealing damage and getting long-range kills. At full stacks, dealing damage will repair your Armor, giving damage-focused players an additional way to stay alive.

The Blue Core focuses on drawing enemy attention and surviving incoming damage. You'll generate more Threat and deal additional damage while out of cover. Build stacks by taking damage and eliminating the enemy that last hit you. At full stacks, dealing damage has a chance to apply Shock, with the chance based on your Skill Tier.

The Yellow Core rewards status-effect builds. You'll deal more weapon damage to enemies affected by status effects, while applying status effects and eliminating affected enemies builds your stacks. At full stacks, your group gains Damage to Armor based on your Critical Damage.

But there's another challenge: enemies are randomly assigned Red, Blue, or Yellow colors, and each color comes with its own combat effect. You'll need to understand those enemy mechanics and coordinate your build to maximize your Player Rating.

Découvrez l'un des setups hybrides les plus puissants du nouveau DLC Echoes of Central Park sur The Division 2 ! En combinant le set d'équipement Core Strength, les redoutables Gants de Manès (obtenus en éliminant les 4 Chasseurs du DLC), le sac à dos exotique NinjaBike Messenger et la nouvelle compétence du Drone Trophy System, ce build offre un équilibre redoutable entre gros dégâts et défense active, tout en vous permettant de garder une arme principale (comme le Capacitor) en main.

Retrouvez ci-dessous le détail complet des pièces, des attributs et des horaires de la vidéo pour tout reproduire facilement.

🛠️ DÉTAIL DU BUILD & ÉQUIPEMENT :

Spécialisation : Technicien (pour le palier de compétence supplémentaire et la synergie avec la ruche)

Arme principale : Capacitor (ou Ratel / Saint-Elme selon vos préférences)

Set Core Strength (3 pièces — Masque, Torse, Genouillères) :

Masque : Attribut principal en Tiers de compétence

Torse : Attribut principal en Tiers de compétence

Genouillères : Attribut principal en Dégâts d'armes

Sac à dos : NinjaBike Messenger (Exotique — fait office de raccord pour valider les bonus de set et apporte un tiers de chaque catégorie)

Gants : Gants de Manès (Marque Walker & Harris, obtenus après avoir éliminé les 4 Chasseurs du DLC Central Park — attributs full rouge en dégâts d'armes, offrant des bonus massifs de dégâts aux protections).

Holster : Picaros (Attribut principal en Tiers de compétence, +10 % de dégâts d'armes, attribut secondaire en dégâts de coups critiques, combiné au NinjaBike pour atteindre les 6 Tiers de compétence).

Compétences :

Drone Trophy System : Possède une probabilité d'intercepter les projectiles ennemis et une probabilité de renvoyer uniquement les tirs adverses, tout en vous laissant libre d'utiliser votre fusil d'assaut.

Ruche Artificier : Spécialisation Technicien pour booster et maintenir la compétence active.

⏱️ CHAPITRES & HORODATAGES :

- Perfect Tag Team

Expand for Loadout:

Mask - Fenris | Amalgam | Crit Chance/Weapon Handling | Crit Damage Mod
Chest -  Equalizer(Unit Alloys) | Echo | Crit Chance/Weapon Handling | Crit Damage Mod
Backpack - Unit Alloys | Vigilance | Crit Chance/Weapon Handling | Crit Damage Mod
Gloves - Rugged Gauntlets | Crit Chance/Crit Damage
Holster - Salvo(Unit Alloys) [Armor Core] | Rate of Fire/Weapon Handling
Kneepads - Fenris | Crit Chance/Weapon Handling

Primary - Ratel
Secondary - First Bloom

Specialization - Gunner

Built Thought Process:

*Always try to swap weapons to get a kill to clean the Joker debuff. Don't be like me and be stubborn trying to power through it.

I have 3pc Unit Alloy builds for Chameleon and Bighorn with slight differences for the other 3 pieces. This variation is for the Ratel to really lean in on the mag size bonus. For those that don't know, the Ratel's bonus is dependent on building stacks by landing 100 shots for each stack. Each stack provides a 20% damage bonus that scales with the enemies missing armor. No missing armor, stacks deal 0% damage, but as the enemy loses armor/health, the damage will scale up to the max. Stripped of armor, the 1st stack now does 10% damage and at 4 stacks, this will do 40% damage in this scenario. So it's a reverse First Bloom.

You also lose stacks if you don't fire ONE shot or reload within a 7 second time frame. So I tend to fire a shot, run for a bout 5 seconds and reload, then run for another 5 seconds and fire a shot, and repeat in between encounters (this can be annoying especially longer breaks). Also stacks are lost when weapon swapping. So ideally, you want to never swap from the Ratel and I don't in the gameplay, but that's usually a bad idea because of the current Mutators for Escalation. Joker stack debuffs your weapon damage and is supposed to promote weapon swapping to clear the stacks. I decided I wanted to try and power through that with the Ratel. It worked, but I definitely felt the lower damage.

1b8227g.text: The Division 2 launched in March 2019 with stray dogs all over its ruined city, and the only thing you could do to them was shoot them. On March 6, 2019 a player started the Can You Pet the Dog? account, which checks one thing about every game, and within weeks it had well over a hundred thousand followers. When it told Enter the Gungeon that you could not pet the dog, designer Dave Crooks added petting in the game's next update "as a direct response", because "it was a label we couldn't live with." A year later, The Division 2: Warlords of New York put a German Shepherd puppy in the players' base, the first dog the game lets you pet, and the account finally got to post the answer it wanted. Agents, crossplay is finally coming to The Division Two across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox! The latest maintenance marks the final stage of Ubisoft's Crossplay rollout, bringing players together across all three platforms and making it easier than ever to squad up with friends, no matter where they play.

PC players were already migrated to the new Crossplay servers on November tenth. Now, on November seventeenth, PlayStation and Xbox players will join those servers, and full Crossplay matchmaking will become available. This means Agents on PC, PlayStation, and Xbox can finally play together!

Crossplay will be enabled by default, but players who prefer to stay on their own platform can turn it off from the Character Selection screen. Ubisoft is also increasing the Clan member limit from fifty to one hundred, giving communities more room to grow and bring Agents together.

There are a few other changes worth knowing about. Leaderboards will become available again when Crossplay launches, and existing Clans will migrate automatically as their first member joins the new servers. However, Clan messages, invitations, join requests, and Clan caches will not carry over during the migration.

18mtcnx.text:
This Legendary Fafnir Trophy System build is the close-range Core Strength hybrid I’ve been tweaking for you: six skill tiers, no shield, 2.1 million armor. Let them shoot — the Trophy System sends it back.

If you loved the tank Core Strength Fafnir at 2.7 million armor with a shield, you didn’t waste that work. This is the other side of the same idea — a skill-damage, crowd-control, shotgun hybrid that lives at close range. Trophy System, The Howl, and Anomaly keep you standing off skill damage. I’m only showing Legendary gameplay, solo and in a group. No modifiers on this one. And with the Assault event live — up to a 200% close-range damage multiplier — this pairing is right where the build already wants to be.

The trade is real: when the skills are down and you’re out of cover, it gets dangerous. Keep the drone up, keep the Howl in the rotation, and let the shotgun work inside that window.

Want to appreciate some of the viewers on my last video for pointing out a small mistake. I was pretty tired from work and just forgot to flip a core. Uploading a new video with a corrected build to keep myself accountable and responsive to YOU!
